The keynote, on behalf of the Inspector-General of Police, Mr. Tunji Disu, was delivered by the Lagos State Commissioner of Police, Mr. Fatai Tijani. But beyond titles and protocol, the message was one: Nigeria must stop waiting for the next abduction before it acts. The Chairperson’s Warning: Don’t stop at the press statement. Prof. Ogundipe, as chairperson, set the tone. He did not want another conference of communiques. When funds are allocated, we should investigate whether they are used as intended, and when investigations produce recommendations, we should return to determine what has changed,” he said. “Our ultimate objective is not to embarrass institutions. It is to ensure that they fulfil their responsibilities.” For a country where security votes and intervention funds often disappear into vague budget lines, it was a pointed call for accountability journalism. “Children are not safe until every school is safe” If Ogundipe gave the framework, EWAN Chairman, Mojeed Alabi, gave the conscience. Standing before his colleagues, Alabi began with a line that would echo through the hall all day: Children are not safe until every school is safe. “No parent should have to choose between a child’s education and their safety. No teacher should have to teach under the shadow of abduction, and no community should have to watch its future disappear because its schools have become targets,” he said. In a deeply personal address titled: Why Journalism Matters in the Fight Against Violent Attacks on Schools, Alabi traced the pattern Nigerians have come to know too well: an attack happens, government issues a statement, security agencies announce interventions, public outrage rises, then attention moves elsewhere – until the next attack. “We must therefore ask: how many more warnings, disrupted school terms and grieving families will it take before school safety becomes an unquestionable national priority?” he asked. His answer was journalism that makes the invisible visible. Not just reporting the number of children abducted, but asking whether the school had a functional emergency response system. Whether teachers had safety training. Whether there was a channel to report threats. How many school days were lost. Whether survivors returned to school. What support they got. “Behind every school attack are human lives. Children must never be reduced to statistics or used merely to provoke sympathy. Their stories deserve accuracy, dignity, sensitivity and appropriate protection of their identities,” Alabi said. “We cannot promise that journalism alone will end attacks on schools but journalism can ensure that warning signs are not ignored, public resources are scrutinised, failures are exposed, promises are tracked and affected communities are heard.” It was a call for newsrooms to invest in expertise, collaborate with researchers, and use radio, television, newspapers and digital platforms to reach communities often excluded from national conversations. He outlined four pillars: intelligence-led policing and early warning, stronger police-community partnerships, improved preparedness and coordinated response, and professionalism with respect for human rights. And he had a warning for journalists too: “The need for speed in journalism must never displace the obligation to accuracy.” Sensational headlines, he said, can compromise rescue efforts and endanger children. item.title: Ebola: Atiku challenges Tinubu to account for N10bn
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has challenged President Bola Tinubu to account for the N10 billion announced for Ebola preparedness, alleging that the confirmed case in Abuja exposed serious gaps in surveillance and the protection of health workers. Atiku said the government must explain how the emergency funds were spent and why the response allegedly left frontline health workers without adequate protective equipment. He also warned against using the outbreak to restrict political campaigns and voter participation. In a statement by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the ADC Presidential Campaign Council, on Wednesday, Atiku demanded a public audit of the funds and answers over the handling of the case. “Where is the money? Publish the amount actually disbursed, the dates of payment, every contract awarded, every recipient and every item delivered. A press statement cannot replace an audit,” he said. Atiku said the patient arrived in Nigeria on October 5, developed symptoms on October 7 and sought treatment at a private hospital on October 11, but the government did not publicly confirm the case until October 20. “During that critical period, 44 close contacts were left unmonitored, while private health workers faced the case without adequate protective equipment. This is a failure of preparedness with potentially grave consequences,” he said. He also questioned the Presidential Task Force announced by Tinubu in June and chaired by his Chief of Staff, Femi Gbajabiamila, insisting that medical experts should lead the response. “Political titles cannot trace contacts, equip hospitals or save lives,” Atiku said. The former vice president further alleged that the planned press conference by the Minister of Health on Thursday was intended to discourage Nigerians from attending campaign rallies and voting. “The Tinubu administration must not weaponise Ebola to frighten the public, silence its opponents or suppress voter participation. Any public health measure must be backed by clear medical evidence, applied equally and never used as a pretext to interfere with Nigerians’ democratic rights,” he said. Atiku urged the government to account for the N10 billion, protect health workers and trace all contacts, warning against turning a public health emergency into a tool for political suppression. item.title: Insurance firms’ N300b stuck at CBN over verification for illicit funds
item.description: By Rosemary Iwunze Insurance companies are now struggling to have access to the new capital they raised, amounting to about N300 billion under the just concluded recapitalization programme. The funds were held in the Central Bank of Nigeria, CBN, pending verifications for illicit funds inflows. Vanguard learnt that following suspicion of possible illicit sources of some of the new investments in the firms the apex imposed stricter capital verification regime, a development which has proved tough for most of the insurance firms to scale through. It is further learnt that while the National Insurance Commission, NAICOM, has given approval for the apex bank to release the funds to the insurers, the affected firms are painstakingly going through the processes. Speaking to journalist during the virtual press briefing on the outcome of the Insurers Committee meeting, Chairman of Nigeria Insurers Association, NIA, Mrs. Ebelechukwu Nwachukwu, stated that, the insurance sector regulator has done its part while operators are currently working on the CBN criteria to access the funds on or before the end of this month. The insurers said they had planned to deploy the new capital in the third quarter of this year to boost their financial performance in 2026 while rewarding their investors with good returns in dividend for their support in the recapitalization program. Recall that the 24 insurance companies had cumulatively raised N300 billion during the exercise, added to over N700 billion existing capital, taking the total industry capital to N1.079 trillion, post recapitalisation. The Nigerian Insurance Industry Reform Act (NIIRA), 2025, had stipulated that the underwriting firms and reinsurers who participated in the recapitalisation exercise that ended on July 31st, 2026 must keep their recapitalised funds in an escrow account with CBN. Of the 50 firms that scaled through the recapitalisation hurdle, 24 of them raised fresh capital while 26 of them had earlier surpassed the minimum capital benchmark. NIIRA had mandated life underwriters to recapitalise from N2billion to N10billion, non-life from N3billion to N15billion while reinsurers were required to upgrade from N10billion to N35billion. The Commissioner for Insurance/CEO, NAICOM, Mr. Olusegun Omosehin, had earlier disclosed that the capital in the market has now risen to N1.079trillion, up from about N700billion before the exercise. According to him, NAICOM now wants to allow operators access the recapitalisation funds, he promised that the regulator would monitor the operators to ensure that the funds fulfill its purpose and not mismanaged or divested into something else. item.title: Ebola patient arrived Abuja Oct. 3 via Ethiopian Airlines from Uganda – Source
item.description: By Omeiza Ajayi Fresh facts emerged, yesterday, regarding the travel itinerary of the confirmed Ebola virus patient in the Federal Capital Territory, FCT, revealing that the index case entered Nigeria aboard an Ethiopian Airlines flight earlier this month. Read Also: No vaccine, specific treatment for Ebola strain in Nigeria — WHO A highly-placed aviation official, who spoke on the condition of anonymity, as she was not authorised to brief the media on the matter, told Vanguard that the patient arrived in the country on October 3, 2026. This is even as the Ugandan government asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the woman, the index case, insisting she didn’t pick the virus in its territory, since there is no Ebola case in Uganda. According to the aviation official, the patient landed at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, aboard Ethiopian Airlines Flight ET333. The revelation provides critical details for contact-tracing, following an earlier official announcement by the Coordinating Minister of Health and Social Welfare, Professor Muhammad Pate, who confirmed the presence of the virus in the nation’s capital. Pate had disclosed that the female patient had recently returned to Nigeria on an international flight from Uganda and subsequently spent several days receiving care at a private hospital in Abuja before the infection was formally diagnosed. She has since been transferred to a designated isolation facility where she is currently receiving treatment. In response, a multi-agency operation involving the Federal Ministry of Health, the Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention, NCDC, and the FCT Health and Environmental Services Secretariat has commenced extensive contact-tracing. Public health authorities have so far identified 44 close contacts, including healthcare personnel, fellow hospital patients, caregivers and individuals connected to her travel route. Consequently, the Federal Government has placed health institutions and port health surveillance units across the country on high alert. Nigeria confirms first Ebola case is Bundibugyo strain The first Ebola case detected in Nigeria is the Bundibugyo strain, an emergency meeting on the issue was told yesterday. “We did three levels of tests, but all molecular. The strain was Bundibugyo,” Olajumoke Babatunde, Director of the Public Health Laboratory Service at NCDC, said yesterday. The World Health Organization, WHO, which also confirmed that it was the Bundibugyo strain, for which there is still neither a vaccine nor a specific treatment. “This person is actually a diplomat,” another official said, adding the patient had deteriorated into “multi-organ failure”. The official did not disclose the nationality of the diplomat. In August, Uganda was declared officially Ebola-free by WHO after recording 20 cases, almost all people who had travelled from the DRC. Uganda seeks details of Nigeria’s confirmed Ebola case In a related development, Uganda has asked Nigeria to provide detailed travel and clinical records of the index case in the country. The Federal Government had confirmed on Tuesday that the woman recently arrived in Nigeria after travelling from Uganda. But in a statement, Director-General of Health Services, Uganda Ministry of Health, Prof. Charles Olaro, said the information is required to guide further investigations and determine whether additional contact-tracing was necessary, even as he stressed that the woman’s transit through Uganda did not establish that she contracted the virus there. The statement, issued in Kampala, said the Ministry of Health is awaiting further information from the Nigerian government to help establish the circumstances surrounding the infection, adding that it would strengthen screening and other public health measures at points of entry in collaboration with relevant agencies. Preliminary information cited by the Ugandan authorities revealed that the woman, who travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business, transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms, but reportedly developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria, as the location where she contracted the virus remained under investigation. The statement, titled “Reported Ebola Case in Nigeria: Ministry Calls for Calm and Vigilance” read: “The Ministry of Health has noted reports of a confirmed Ebola case in Nigeria involving a Nigerian woman who reportedly travelled to the eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo for business. “Preliminary information indicates that she transited through Uganda in early October without showing symptoms and developed symptoms after arriving in Nigeria. Her transit through Uganda does not establish that she contracted the infection there. Personalities at the convocation include the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji, Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Enitan Ogunwusi, Ojaja II; the Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe; the Ogoga of Ikere-Ekiti, Oba Samuel Adu Adejimi and the Olowo of Owo Kingdom, Oba Ajibade Gbadegesin Ogunoye III. Others are the Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, SAN; Dr Wole Oluyede, the Peoples Democratic Party (PDP) governorship candidate in Ekiti State; Chief Wole Olanipekun, SAN; and former Governor of Ekiti State, Engr Segun Oni. Speaking at the convocation ceremony, the Governor of Ekiti State, Biodun Oyebanji hailed Olajide for his investments in agriculture, tourism and other sectors of Ekiti State’s economy, while Okonkwo was recognised for his contributions to business and enterprise development. He also described the duo as accomplished international entrepreneurs who had complemented the state government’s drive to attract private investment, generate employment and accelerate industrialisation. The governor said Olajide, through Cavista Holdings, the parent company of Agbeyewa Farms and Glocient Hospitality, had committed millions of dollars to the state’s economy, with significant investments in agriculture, hospitality and tourism. He also added that Professor Obiora’s investment in aviation, made it possible for Ekiti State to record over 10,000 passengers at the Ekiti Cargo Allied International Airport since the commencement of the commercial flights in December 10, 2025. “I want to sincerely extend the same congratulatory message to my brother, Mr. John Niyi Olajide, an accomplished innovator, international businessman and a passionate Ekiti compatriot. Even though, he has made good fortunes for himself abroad, he has joined in the vision of our government to promote private investment and industrialize the State. “Through his Cavista Holdings, the parent owners of Agbeyewa Farms and Glocient Hospitality, he has invested millions of dollars in Ekiti economy, employing hundreds of people and transforming both the agriculture and tourism landscape of Ekiti State. He is in charge of the ongoing transformation of Ikogosi Warm Spring Resorts to a world class tourist destination. “Today, Niyi John Olajide is the second biggest investor in Ekiti after Aare Afe Babalola. His investments through Cavista Holdings has employed thousands of Ekiti people through his investment in Agbeyewa Farms, the biggest cassava farm in the world and through his transformative impact at Ikogosi Warm Spring that has turned the corridor to the world renowned Holiday Resort in Nigeria”. He added The Ooni of Ife, Oba Adeyeye Ogunwusi, also praised the duo’s achievements, describing them as outstanding personalities whose commitment to job creation and entrepreneurship deserve recognition. The Ewi of Ado-Ekiti, Oba Rufus Adejugbe, called for greater private-sector participation in the state’s development, noting that Ekiti needed more entrepreneurs willing to commit their resources, expertise and experience to building its economy. The monarch said the state had long looked forward to attracting more investors to complement the developmental contributions of ABUAD founder, Aare Afe Babalola. Other highlight of the event was the conferment of honorary Doctor of Laws degrees on the founder of the University, Aare Afe Babalola by the representatives of Trinity Western University, Canada, and Trinity International University, United States, for his contributions in several sector such as education, health, law, agriculture, among others In his remarks, Aare Afe Babalola described the convocation as the best moment of his life, urging the graduating students to be good ambassadors of the university and become problem solvers. In their responses, the honorees commended the contributions of Aare Afe Babalola towards the development of the state and the country, with a pledge to continue to use their goodwills for the development of Ekiti and Nigeria at large. Giving the breakdown of the 2,194 graduands, 1,759 completed undergraduate and professional programmes, while 435 agraduated from postgraduate programmes, comprising 359 students of the College of Postgraduate Studies and 76 from the ABUAD Business School’s postgraduate programmes. 286 graduands obtained First Class degrees, while 824 earned Second Class Upper degrees. Another 234 obtained Second Class Lower degrees, while 29 graduated with Third Class degrees. The remaining graduands completed professional or postgraduate programmes to which the conventional degree classifications do not apply. Photo: Kehinde Gbadamosi. The gathering, which brought together prominent figures from the labour movement and the radical civil society, transcended a mere remembrance of the late activist, and became a platform for soul-searching, renewed commitment and a frank assessment of the challenges confronting the Nigeria left. Speakers, including Nigeria Labour Congress, NLC, President, Joe Ajaero; human rights lawyer, Femi Falana, SAN; President of the Academic Staff Union of Universities, ASUU, Prof. Christopher Piwuna; and other labour and civil society leaders, stressed the need to move beyond rhetoric, fragmented struggles and periodic protests towards building a formidable mass movement capable of effecting fundamental political and economic transformation. At the heart of the deliberations was the need to rebuild LASCO, an alliance of trade unions and pro-labour civil society organisations under the umbrella of the Joint Action Front, JAF, of which the late Aremu was secretary. The coalition played a prominent role in mobilising resistance against policies perceived as inimical to the interests of workers and ordinary Nigerians. Participants also underscored the urgency of linking workplace struggles with the broader quest for political power, with proposals for a new revolutionary political party, stronger grassroots mobilisation and sustained mass action emerging as key elements of the way forward. Against the backdrop of the 2027 general elections, the memorial became more than an occasion to honour Aremu’s legacy; it was also a renewed challenge to the labour movement and the Nigerian left to overcome internal divisions, reclaim their political initiative and translate years of agitation into an organised force for change. Way forward Speaking, Ajaero, who was represented by NLC’s Acting General Secretary, Benson Upah, argued that a united front, mass mobilisation and the establishment of alternative institutions were critical to advancing the struggle for political and economic transformation. According to him: “The way forward requires building a united front to overcome the fragmentation of the Nigerian left and labour movement, forging a common platform through honest debate. We must escalate our struggle beyond ultimatums, mobilising millions of workers, students, and community members. “We must build alternative institutions; our own media, research bodies, educational programmes, and cooperative enterprises; to counter the ruling class’ control of the state, media, and universities. “We must link the economic struggle to the political struggle, demanding not just lower fuel prices but a fundamental restructuring of the economy to serve the many, not the few, and organising around the 2027 general elections. “Finally, we must be internationalist, building solidarity with workers and oppressed peoples worldwide and opposing imperialism in all its forms. “Only through such a comprehensive strategy can the working class and masses challenge the neo-liberal order and advance toward genuine liberation. The task is formidable, but the alternative; continued immiseration, repression, and despair; is unacceptable. United, organised, and determined, we can build a movement capable of winning.” A new movement coming Similarly, Falana, SAN, announced plans to launch a movement that could eventually evolve into a revolutionary political party capable of contesting and winning political power in Nigeria. “Let me also announce that, following the challenges we confronted last year after the passing of our comrade, the burial committee has continued to meet and reflect on the state of the nation. “A movement will soon be formally launched. The objective is to develop this movement into a revolutionary political party capable of contesting and winning political power in Nigeria. “We can organise countless symposia, rallies and demonstrations, but we must also address the question of how political power is acquired and exercised. “The ruling class understands that power cannot be won through social media alone. It must be built through organisation, collective action and sustained engagement with the people.” LP failed to deliver change On his part, the ASUU president, Prof. Christopher Piwuna, questioned whether the objectives Aremu pursued during his lifetime had been achieved, arguing that the struggle for systemic change remained far from its goal. He queried: “I have often wondered whether, over the past year, Comrade Aremu’s objectives have been achieved and whether we have fulfilled the promises we made after his passing. “After listening to earlier speakers, I am convinced that we still have a great deal of work to do. “Comrade Aremu wanted the system to change. He advocated, struggled and devoted his life to that objective. “From what we have heard today, we have not even succeeded in changing our own political party. “The Labour Party, LP, was supposed to be the vehicle through which we would challenge the existing system. We must ask ourselves whether we have effectively resisted the forces oppressing the Nigerian people through mass action. All of us must accept responsibility for the party’s failure. “Every day, new political leaders emerge who reproduce the same patterns of oppression. We continue to see more people who behave like Tinubu and more who follow the political patterns associated with Peter Obi. “We have gathered here not merely to lament but to renew our commitment to the struggle. The system has not changed, and the mass action required to transform it has not yet reached the scale necessary to achieve our objectives.” Revival of LASCO In the same vein, Rashidat Adesina of JAF called for the revival of LASCO as an organised platform for cooperation between trade unions and radical, pro-labour civil society organisations. She said: “We previously had the Labour and Civil Society Coalition, known as LASCO. It provided a platform for cooperation between trade unions and radical, pro-labour civil society organisations. What has happened to that coalition? “It was an important instrument of resistance. Although meetings have taken place, there has been insufficient concrete action to rebuild it. We must revive LASCO, not as a ceremonial alliance, but as an organised force rooted in trade unions and working-class communities. “We must also confront the influence of ethnic and regional politics within the labour movement. When political support is based on personality, ethnicity or regional affiliation, it becomes easier for the ruling class to divide workers. “President Bola Tinubu, Atiku Abubakar and Peter Obi may have differences during election campaigns, but when mass movements threaten the interests of private capital, powerful interests can unite against those movements. item.description: By Adesina Wahab Teachers of the International School, University of Lagos (ISL), on Wednesday began a work-to-rule action over delays in implementing a National Industrial Court judgment, payment of outstanding salary arrears and restoration of their names to the university’s payroll. The teachers are demanding the implementation of the court judgment, payment of outstanding Consolidated Tertiary Institutions Teaching Allowance (CONTTA) arrears and the 2024 arrears arising from the 25 per cent and 35 per cent salary adjustments. Addressing the teachers during a protest on campus, the Chairman of the Senior Staff Association of Nigerian Universities (SSANU), University of Lagos branch, Comrade Razak Yusuf, said the action followed prolonged delays in resolving issues concerning the teachers’ employment status and financial entitlements. Yusuf noted that a similar dispute involving teachers at the University of Abuja had been resolved by the Federal Government following a court judgment. The teachers said the work-to-rule action was not an abandonment of their teaching responsibilities but a response to unresolved employment and welfare concerns. They maintained that their appointment letters and years of service established their employment relationship with the university, arguing that their posting to the International School did not absolve the institution of its responsibilities as their employer. item.title: FUTATH mourns Fasoranti, describes him as dependable voice for justice, equity, federalism
item.description: — Says role in FUTA teaching hospital will be remembered – CMD By Dayo Johnson Akure The Federal University of Technology Akure Teaching Hospital (FUTATH) has mourned the death of Afenifere leader, Pa Reuben Fasoranti, describing him as a dependable voice for justice, equity, true federalism and good governance. The Chief Medical Director (CMD) of the Teaching Hospital, Prof. Olusegun Ojo, in a statement he personally signed, condoled with the family of the elder statesman over his passage. The statement reads: “With heavy hearts but profound gratitude to God for an uncommon life of service, we commiserate with the immediate family of Pa Reuben Famuyide Fasoranti, the leadership and members of Afenifere, the good people of Akure, Ondo State, and the entire nation over the passage of this revered elder statesman, who died yesterday at the old and ripe age of 100 years. “Pa Fasoranti was a teacher, school administrator, politician, pro-democracy activist, and a dependable voice for justice, equity, true federalism, and good governance. “As a former Commissioner for Finance in the old Ondo State and, for many years, the leader of Afenifere, he served with integrity, courage, and an enduring commitment to the progress of the Yoruba people and Nigeria. “Beyond public service, Baba was a visionary educationist whose legacy lives on through the schools he established, including Omolere Nursery and Primary School, Akure High School, and St. Frances’ Academy, Igoba. “He shaped generations of learners and demonstrated, throughout his life, that leadership is best measured by the opportunities one creates for others. “We particularly recall with deep appreciation his pivotal role in the actualisation of the FUTA Teaching Hospital, Akure. “His advocacy, credibility, fatherly intervention, and personal engagement with the Federal Government were instrumental in bringing the long-awaited teaching hospital to Akure. “This singular contribution will continue to strengthen medical education, healthcare delivery, and specialist care for the people of Ondo State and beyond. “Pa Fasoranti lived a full, purposeful, and impactful life. He was a bridge-builder, a defender of the voiceless, and a rare statesman whose counsel transcended politics. ” Though we mourn his physical departure, we take comfort in the enduring institutions, ideals, and lives he touched.” Prof. Ojo prayed for the family of the late Yoruba leader who died on Tuesday, October 20, 2026 at his residence in Akure, the Ondo State capital. “We pray that God will grant his immediate family, Afenifere, and all who mourn him the fortitude to bear this irreparable loss,” he said. The CMD prayed that “May his gentle soul find eternal rest, and may his legacy of service, education, justice, and nation-building continue to inspire present and future generations.” The post FUTATH mourns Fasoranti, describes him as dependable voice for justice, equity, federalism appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police arrest three suspects, recover gun in Jigawa
item.description: By Muhammad Inuwa, Dutse The Jigawa State Police Command has arrested three suspects and recovered a locally fabricated pistol, ammunition and other weapons along the Nguru–Birniwa Road. The command’s spokesperson, SP Lawan Shiisu Adam, confirmed the arrests in a statement made available to journalists. He said operatives of Operation Salama apprehended the suspects on October 14, 2026, at about 4.30 p.m. during a security patrol. The suspects were identified as Bello Juli, 22; Abdullahi Yakubu, 30; and Bashir Muhammad, 25. All three are from Kyarana Settlement in Kiru Local Government Area of Kano State. According to the police spokesperson, items recovered during the operation included a locally fabricated pistol, three bullets, machetes, bows and arrows, and gunpowder. Adam said the suspects had been charged to court following investigations by the State Criminal Investigation Department in Dutse. Meanwhile, the Commissioner of Police, CP Tijjani Murtala, commended the officers involved in the operation and urged personnel across the command to strengthen surveillance and intelligence gathering to combat criminal activities. He also appealed to members of the public to support security agencies by providing timely information about suspicious individuals and activities in their communities. The command assured residents of its continued commitment to maintaining peace and security across Jigawa State. item.title: EFCC chairman, Mbah, Umahi to grace Enugu NUJ Press Week
item.description: By Anayo Okoli ENUGU — The Chairman of the Economic and Financial Crimes Commission (EFCC), Ola Olukoyede; Enugu State Governor, Peter Mbah; and the Minister of Works, David Umahi, are among the dignitaries expected at the grand finale of the 2026 Press Week of the Enugu State Correspondents’ Chapel of the Nigeria Union of Journalists (NUJ) on Wednesday. The event, scheduled to hold at the Lawrence Ugwuanyi Press Centre, Enugu, will feature discussions on responsible journalism, democratic development and the media’s role in the fight against corruption. Umahi will deliver the guest lecture, while Olukoyede will give the keynote address at the ceremony, which is expected to attract media professionals, government officials, political leaders, security chiefs and other stakeholders. In a statement signed by the Chairman and Secretary of the Press Week Organising Committee, Emma Ugwueze and Damian Duruiheoma, respectively, the committee said the topics were carefully selected to address critical issues affecting the country. It said Umahi and Olukoyede were chosen in recognition of their respective roles in public service, particularly the minister’s efforts in road infrastructure development and the EFCC chairman’s leadership of the country’s anti-corruption campaign. “While Engr. David Umahi, the Honourable Minister of Works, is making visible efforts towards the rehabilitation and revitalisation of several roads across the country, the EFCC Chairman, Olukoyede, has also introduced reforms aimed at strengthening the operations of the anti-graft commission,” the statement said. Umahi’s lecture will focus on the theme, “Strengthening Democracy Through Responsible Journalism: 2027 Polls in Focus,” while Olukoyede will speak on “The Role of the Media and Other Critical Stakeholders in Sustaining the Fight Against Corruption.” The former Enugu State Attorney-General and Commissioner for Justice, Chief Anthony Ani, SAN, will chair the event. Among those expected to receive awards are the Deputy National Chairman (South) of the All Progressives Congress, Dr Ben Nwoye; the Executive Director of the Projects Development Institute (PRODA), Enugu, Dr Peter Okwudilichukwu Ogbobe; and the Enugu State Commissioner of Police, CP Mamman Bitrus Giwa. Others are the Commissioner representing Enugu State at the Federal Character Commission, Peter Eze; the General Manager of Rangers International Football Club, Amobi Ezeaku; and medical expert Dr Celestine Chijioke Ugwuoke, among other recipients. The grand finale will conclude a series of activities organised by the chapel to mark the 2026 Press Week. The programme commenced on Sunday, October 18, with a thanksgiving service at the Christian Victory Prayer Ministry, popularly known as Precious Church, in Enugu. The bill resolves this inconsistency. Clause 18 repeals both provisions. Part II sets out the rights of persons who have attempted suicide, including confidentiality, informed consent, access to legal representation and protection from torture and cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. The bill also provides for a Suicide Prevention Unit, national and state surveillance systems, 24-hour crisis helplines and mandatory training for health workers, law enforcement and correctional personnel. The bill drew support from several senators. Senator Dayo Faduyile, a medical doctor, noted that some survivors have subsequently died by suicide while in detention. The bill has been referred to the Committees on Health and on Judiciary, Human Rights and Legal Matters for a public hearing. Nigeria’s human rights obligations The question is not solely one of health policy. Nigeria has accepted binding obligations that bear directly on it. UN Special Rapporteurs on the right to health and on torture have found the criminalisation of suicide attempts inconsistent with these obligations, noting that the detention of persons in acute distress may engage the prohibition of cruel, inhuman or degrading treatment. The World Health Organization identifies decriminalisation as a critical step towards the Sustainable Development Goal target of reducing suicide mortality by one third by 2030. From an international human rights and legal standpoint, penalising attempted suicide is fundamentally flawed, counterproductive, and inconsistent with Nigeria’s treaty obligations under international law. Criminalisation undermines the right to health and life As a State party to the International Covenant on Economic, Social and Cultural Rights, Nigeria must respect, protect and fulfil the right to the highest attainable standard of physical and mental health under Article 12. Incarceration exacerbates psychological suffering, stripping individuals of their agency at their most vulnerable moment rather than providing therapeutic care. Distortion of public health data and interventions. Decriminalisation is a prerequisite for effective public health governance. When suicide attempts are illegal, official data severely underreports the true scale of the mental health crisis in Nigeria. item.title: 2027: The Strength Of APC Is In Northern Nigeria – Basiru
item.description: The National Secretary of the All Progressives Congress (APC), Senator Ajibola Basiru, has described Northern Nigeria as the ruling party’s stronghold ahead of the 2027 general elections, insisting that both the region’s political elite and ordinary citizens support the party. Speaking on Channels Television’s Politics Today on Wednesday, Basiru expressed confidence in the APC’s prospects in the North, citing the support of prominent political figures and the establishment of a campaign office known as Arewa for Asiwaju. “The strength of the APC is in the Northern part of this country and you will see it by the grace of God when election comes in 2027. On Saturday, we had the leading lights in politics, in economy, in industry gathering together to donate a campaign office they call Arewa for Asiwaju. “Even some who are in the opposition party have changed, people like the former governor of Niger State Babangida Aliyu, now all of them are coming to join and work for the APC. The truth is that today, when you see the creme de la creme of Northern Nigeria, they are with us, you see the masses of Northern Nigeria are with us,” Basiru said. ﻿ The APC National Secretary also criticised opposition parties over their response to electoral defeats, saying they should learn to accept losses as part of the democratic process. Basiru said President Bola Tinubu had emphasised the need for politicians to accept both victory and defeat, adding that the APC had experienced losses in court cases and political contests but had moved on. “One of the things that our leader President Bola Ahmed Tinubu said is that anybody that wants that savour the joy of victory in a democracy must also be able to endure the pain when he loses. But in the case of Nigeria, it appears that the opposition only wants to win, they don’t want to lose. We have had our fair share of losses both in the court and in the political contests, and we have taken it, learn our lessons and moved on,” he said. item.title: Como Humiliate Struggling Manchester United In Champions League Clash
item.description: Manchester United’s struggles deepened with a dismal 4-1 Champions League defeat at Como on Wednesday, piling further pressure on under-fire manager Michael Carrick. Nico Paz’s brilliant double inspired debutants Como to a famous win, with Tasos Douvikas and Jacobo Ramon also on target for the Italians. Only a late Joshua Zirkzee goal spared United from suffering their joint-heaviest defeat in the competition as the crisis-hit visitors’ winless run extended to seven games. United boss Carrick faced mounting pressure after a poor run of three draws and three defeats in all competitions sealed their worst start to a league campaign for 40 years. (From L) Como’s Spanish midfielder #06 Luis Milla, Como’s Croatian midfielder #20 Martin Baturina. Como’s Greek forward #09 Tasos Douvikas and Como’s Spanish defender #03 Alex Valle celebrate after winning the UEFA Champions League, league phase matchday 3, football match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia in Como, northen Italy on October 21, 2026. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP) But a lacklustre Red Devils team failed to muster a response in the wind and rain of northern Italy as they were thoroughly outclassed to remain on three points in the Champions League. Cesc Fabregas’s side have enjoyed a fairytale rise from Serie B to Europe’s elite club competition over the last three years, but their dismantling of the three-time European champions will go down as one of the greatest results in club history. (Photo by Marco BERTORELLO / AFP) Argentina international Paz lit up the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia with superb solo efforts either side of Douvikas’s accomplished finish, before Ramon’s header completed the rout as Como claimed their second win of the league phase to move up to six points. With both sides facing a string of injuries, there was one major surprise in Carrick’s team as defender Matthijs de Ligt returned for his first appearance in 11 months following injury, replacing the suspended Leny Yoro. Diogo Dalot had an early sight at goal when his shot curled inches wide of the far post, but Como immediately went up the other end and showed superior cutting edge. Familiar flaws exposed Manchester United’s players react after receiving 4th goal during the UEFA Champions League, league phase matchday 3, football match between Como 1907 and Manchester United at the Stadio Giuseppe Sinigaglia in Como, northern Italy on October 21, 2026. (Photo by PIERO CRUCIATTI / AFP) Paz received the ball on the edge of the box, shifted it onto his favoured left foot and guided a finish home to give the hosts a dream start inside two minutes. It exposed familiar flaws for United, who conceded inside the opening minute in their 2-0 defeat to Atletico Madrid last week and have now kept one clean sheet in 11 games this season in all competitions. Como’s confidence grew with the lead as they dominated possession and restricted rudderless United to having no shots on target before half-time, while threatening themselves through Douvikas and Martin Baturina. Carrick made a double change at the interval to try and lift a sluggish performance as Amad Diallo and Carlos Baleba replaced Andrey Santos and Matheus Cunha. But they were caught cold once again as Paz slipped a through ball into Douvikas’s path and the Greece international lifted a first-time finish into the top corner three minutes into the second half. Como captain Lucas Da Cunha squandered a promising chance to make it three by shooting wide. But the home crowd did not have to wait long to celebrate again as Paz nicked the ball off a hesitant Baleba in midfield before driving forward and finishing coolly in the 57th minute. A shell-shocked United defence almost conceded a fourth when Paz, eyeing a hat-trick, had a curling effort saved by a diving Senne Lammens. Number four arrived with 14 minutes to go when unmarked centre-back Ramon roamed forward to head home an inviting cross. It sparked an exodus of fans in the away end, who missed substitute Zirkzee’s stoppage-time strike in United’s one bright moment of the evening.
